title: Knowledge check: Advanced Vue Styling

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Advanced Vue Styling”?
options: List movement can be animated reliably without stable identity.
Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Animation should be the only signal for errors.
Scoped styles automatically affect every unrelated component.
questions.answer_key: Use CSS or Vue transitions to communicate a real state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Advanced Vue Styling directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Dynamic style bindings”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Use transitions to communicate a state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
Motion should be the only way to communicate an error.
Scoped styles automatically affect every unrelated component.
Every list can animate correctly without stable keys.
questions.answer_key: Use transitions to communicate a state change and respect reduced-motion preferences.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Dynamic style bindings”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Advanced Vue Styling” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
